issues.t: Front strut upper mounts can break loose (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the top of the front struts, or a front corner that sags or feels loose.
issues.why: The upper mounting bases for the front struts were not strong enough, and the bolts holding them to the body could break. Suzuki recall 00V008000 added reinforcements and replaced the mounts, bolts and strut bar stays.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls with NHTSA or a Suzuki-trained shop. If the front end clunks, have the strut towers inspected before driving far.

issues.t: Fuel tank can be punctured in a rear crash (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs. The risk is a fuel leak after being hit from behind.
issues.why: A reinforcement on the fuel tank flange could puncture the tank in a rear-end crash. Suzuki recall 96V121002 added two shield gussets between the tank and its brackets.
issues.next: Have a shop confirm the recall work was done. If you ever smell fuel, don't drive it until it's checked.

issues.t: Front lower ball joint can separate
issues.sym: Clunking over bumps, wandering or wobbly steering, uneven tire wear. In the worst case a front wheel collapses.
issues.why: The lower ball joints wear and, on rusty trucks, can pull out of the control arm. Suzuki sent US dealers a bulletin stressing inspection and upkeep of these ball joints.
issues.next: Have the ball joints checked at every inspection, especially if you go off-road. Replace any loose joint before driving further.

issues.t: Cooling fan or its bracket breaks and damages the radiator
issues.sym: Rattling or grinding from the front of the engine, loose belts, then the temperature gauge climbs and coolant pours out.
issues.why: Owners report the bracket that carries the cooling fan and A/C compressor cracking, and the fan bearing failing. The loose fan cuts into the radiator and can wreck the A/C compressor too.
issues.next: If the temperature gauge rises, pull over and shut the engine off. Check the fan for wobble and the bracket for cracks at every oil change.

issues.t: Engine stalls when slowing down or turning
issues.sym: The engine dies as you coast to a stop or take your foot off the gas in a turn. It restarts with the key.
issues.why: Owners report stalling while slowing down, after long drives and in four-wheel drive. Fixes reported include a new engine computer and an ignition coil that was shorting. Idle control and sensor faults are other common causes.
issues.next: If it stalls, steer and brake firmly and get off the road. Have a shop check idle control, sensors and ignition parts.

issues.sym: Smoke from under the hood or into the cabin, or a burning plastic smell.
issues.why: Several owners of 1996 Sidekicks reported fires, including one right after turning the key. Electrical shorts and fuel leaks are common causes on older vehicles.
issues.next: If you see smoke or smell burning, stop, turn off the engine and get everyone out. Have the wiring and fuel lines inspected before driving again.

issues.sym: Clunking, vibration or a whine from underneath, or a sudden bang and loss of drive.
issues.why: A 1997 owner reported the driveshaft coming off its mount at about 40 mph, and a 1997 Sidekick Sport owner reported a failed ring and pinion gear set in the differential.
issues.next: Have the U-joints, driveshaft bolts and differential oil checked. A new clunk or vibration under the truck should be inspected right away.

issues.sym: The engine suddenly runs rough or loses power at mid rpm, or won't start.
issues.why: The 1.6L uses a timing belt with a simple tensioner. Owners report belts skipping teeth when the tensioner is set loose or worn, especially after rough trail use.
issues.next: Replace the belt and tensioner together at the recommended interval. If it suddenly runs badly, have the timing marks checked before driving further.

issues.sym: A rattle from the front of the engine, mostly at start-up.
issues.why: The hydraulic timing chain tensioner on the 1.8L can stop holding the chain tight if sludge from skipped oil changes clogs its oil passages. An upgraded tensioner exists.
issues.next: Change the oil on time. If you hear a rattle, have the tensioner checked before the chain wears further.

issues.t: Crankshaft pulley rubber fails and belts slip
issues.sym: Squealing belts, a wobbling pulley, and the engine running hot.
issues.why: The rubber in the crankshaft pulley (harmonic balancer) breaks down with age. The belts then slip and the water pump stops turning properly, so the engine overheats. One 1.8L owner needed a warped head machined after this.
issues.next: If the temperature gauge rises, pull over. Have the crankshaft pulley checked for wobble or cracked rubber.

issues.t: Oil leak from front crankshaft seal
issues.sym: Oil drips under the front of the engine or oil on the belts.
issues.why: The rubber seal around the front of the crankshaft hardens with age and starts to leak.
issues.next: Keep the oil topped up. The seal is easy to replace, and is best done along with the timing belt on the 1.6L.

issues.t: Oil leak at the back of the engine from distributor O-ring
issues.sym: Oil on the back of the engine and the top of the transmission.
issues.why: The large O-ring between the distributor and the cylinder head leaks, often because it was not seated properly when the distributor was last removed.
issues.next: Have the distributor O-ring replaced. It's a cheap part; make sure it sits in its groove when reinstalled.

issues.t: Clutch pedal very stiff or drops to the floor
issues.sym: The clutch pedal is very hard to push, or it suddenly falls to the floor and you can't change gears.
issues.why: A weld on the clutch pedal pivot can break, and RepairPal lists this as the most common Sidekick problem. Owners also report a cracked pedal bracket, a very stiff pedal and a failed clutch slave cylinder.
issues.next: If the pedal feels different or loose, have the pedal bracket and clutch hydraulics checked before the clutch stops working on the road.

issues.t: Check engine light with random codes
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on and the stored codes don't make sense.
issues.why: Suzuki issued bulletin SW02B for the Sidekick Sport: the light can come on with codes that are out of range or don't match any system.
issues.next: Ask a Suzuki-trained shop about bulletin SW02B before replacing parts.

issues.sym: A louder exhaust, ticking or rattling from under the truck.
issues.why: A 1998 Sidekick Sport owner reported exhaust bolts vibrating loose and breaking, along with loose motor mounts.
issues.next: Have the exhaust joints and motor mounts checked. Fix exhaust leaks quickly so fumes don't enter the cabin.
